quick.summary: Why forty reports hide the five that matter, and how to clear the rest.
quick.takeaway: Check who opens it. Ask. Then retire it.

beats.line: We have forty reports. Which ones actually matter?
Look at how often each one is opened.
Most were not opened in three months.
Those still cost you. Every change has to fix them too.
What if someone needs one later?
Ask the owner first, then archive it. It can come back.
Keep the ones opened every week. Review the rest.

board.text: not opened in months: ask, archive

beats.line: Twelve kept. The rest archived, after asking their owners.
Now people find the right report first time.

quiz.question: A report has not been opened in three months. What is the best next step?
options: Ask its owner, then archive it
quiz.explanation: Asking first avoids surprises, and archiving means it can be brought back if needed.

quiz.question: Unused reports cost nothing, so it is fine to keep them all.
quiz.explanation: They still need fixing when data changes, and they make the useful reports harder to find.
